A.title: The Wreck of the Helios Drift
A.description:
Your survey ship drops out of FTL into the wrong sector — dead silent, no beacon, no charted system.
Through the viewport: a massive derelict vessel, dark and drifting, hull scorched by something that burned hotter than any weapon you know.
Your comms are jammed. Your FTL drive needs 40 minutes to spool back up.
The derelict's docking bay is open. Something is moving on the long-range thermal scan.
Three options flicker on your HUD.

AA.title: Breach the Command Deck
AA.description:
You EVA across the void and force your way into the derelict's command deck through a shattered airlock.
Zero-g. Emergency lighting in pulsing red. Consoles gutted — not by explosion but methodically *removed*, as though something needed the components.
On the captain's chair, still strapped in: a skeleton in a pressure suit, visor cracked, fingers frozen mid-gesture toward something on the far wall.
Scrawled in what you choose not to identify: **DO NOT RESPOND TO THE SIGNAL.**

AB.title: Follow the Thermal Signature
AB.description:
The heat source is moving — slowly, deliberately — toward the aft cargo bay.
You match its path through maintenance corridors, mag-boots clicking in the silence.
You find it: a sealed cryo-pod, frost still hissing off the seals, status light cycling green.
Something is waking up inside. The pod's manifest ID has been scratched off. The biological readout shows two heartbeats.

AC.title: Access the Engineering Core
AC.description:
The engineering core is intact — eerie given the rest of the wreck.
The reactor is cold but the auxiliary power grid is alive, fed by something you don't recognise attached to the hull.
On the main terminal, a single open file: a first-contact protocol, partially executed. Coordinates transmitted. Awaiting response.
**Response received: 14 minutes ago.**
Something answered. And the coordinates in the response header match your current position.

BA.title: Override the Transmission Array
BA.description:
The command deck's backup array is still live — barely.
You cross the dead captain's frozen warning, find the transmitter, and burn out the entire system with a sustained power surge.
No more signal. No more beacon. Whatever was coming, it won't find this wreck by its own call.
You EVA back to your ship with six minutes to spare, FTL spooling green.
The derelict shrinks in your rear display. You don't look at it long.

BB.title: Broadcast a Response
BB.description:
The command deck array can do more than receive — you realise the skeleton's gesture was pointing at the broadcast controls.
Maybe diplomacy. Maybe the only way out.
You compose a response in the derelict's own signal format and transmit.
Thirty seconds later, a ship decloaks off your port bow. It is not human-built. It is enormous.
A docking clamp locks onto your hull before you can react.
They are not hostile. But you are not leaving.

BC.title: Open the Cryo-Pod
BC.description:
Two heartbeats. You crack the seals.
Inside: a human woman, mid-thirties, and — wrapped in her arms — something that is almost an infant, if infants had six fingers and eyes that reflect light like a cat's.
She wakes gasping. Her first words: *'Don't let them take it back.'*
Before you can ask anything, the docking bay depressurises. A second ship has attached to the derelict's hull.
They are very fast. They are looking for something specific. They find it.

BD.title: Disconnect the Unknown Device
BD.description:
The thing on the hull is feeding power *to* the derelict — and transmitting. A homing pulse, slow and patient, running for what the logs suggest is eleven years.
You suit up, go outside, and cut it free with a plasma torch. It drifts away, still pulsing, into the dark.
The terminal goes dead. The coordinates in the response header are gone.
You have fourteen minutes until FTL. You spend them watching the scanner. Nothing comes.
Nothing you can detect, anyway.

ESCAPE_ENDING.title: Ghost Jump
ESCAPE_ENDING.description:
FTL spins up. You punch in the first safe coordinates in the database — a fuel depot two systems over, boring, beautiful, and full of other humans.
The derelict vanishes as you jump. No record in your logs of the signal, the coordinates, the response.
You filed it under sensor anomaly. You tell yourself that was the right call.
Some nights you check your own hull for devices you didn't install.
So far, nothing.

✦  YOU ESCAPED  ✦

SACRIFICE_ENDING.title: First Contact
SACRIFICE_ENDING.description:
Their ship is a city. You are processed — gently, thoroughly — over what feels like weeks.
They return you to human space eventually, with no memory of what you told them, and a small scar behind your left ear.
The official debrief finds nothing unusual. You are cleared for active duty.
You never fly solo again. Not because of regulations.
Because you know, now, that you were never really alone out there.

✧  YOUR JOURNEY CONTINUES — SOMEWHERE  ✧

TRAPPED_ENDING.title: Claimed
TRAPPED_ENDING.description:
They are not cruel. They seem, in fact, fascinated.
The woman and the child are taken somewhere else. You are kept separate, studied with instruments that don't touch you, fed, kept warm.
Your ship is still in the docking bay. Untouched. The FTL drive long since spooled down.
You spend a lot of time wondering what the captain's note meant.
You understand it now. You just can't warn anyone.

✧  YOU ARE THEIR GUEST  ✧
